foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Red Sea maritime disruption will sustain energy repricing over the next 30 days, driven by 89% gas supply stress pressure and 82% state confirmation, with Brent crude spiking after the attack on Iran's South Pars...
foil.perspective_strategic: The 89% pressure and 82% state confirmation indicate a durable transmission path through gas supply stress, but the 75% confidence level caps certainty until matched reporting confirms the trajectory.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The absence of more directly matched reporting on Red Sea, combined with the 75% confidence level, could allow the system to revert toward 71% if no new hard signals emerge, as actors prioritize containment over escalation.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 79%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through gas supply stress, with 89% pressure and 82% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
